es.summary: Las estatinas inhiben la HMG‑CoA reductasa, reduciendo la síntesis hepática de colesterol LDL y ofreciendo efectos pleiotrópicos antiinflamatorios y estabilizadores de placa.
key_points: Efectos pleiotrópicos: antiinflamatorio, antioxidante, estabilizador de placa.
Principales efectos adversos: mialgia, rabdomiólisis, elevación de transaminasas.
Contraindicadas en embarazo, lactancia y enfermedad hepática activa.

mechanism: Inhiben la HMG‑CoA reductasa, bloqueando la conversión de HMG‑CoA a mevalonato.
Disminuyen la producción hepática de colesterol y aumentan la expresión de receptores LDL.
Mayor captación de LDL‑c por el hígado reduce su concentración plasmática.
indications: Prevención primaria y secundaria de enfermedad cardiovascular aterosclerótica.
contraindications: Enfermedad hepática activa (ALT/AST >3× límite superior normal).
adverse_effects: Rabdomiólisis (serio) → CK >10 × normal, dolor muscular intenso, orina oscura.
interactions: Inhibidores de CYP3A4 (ej. claritromicina, itraconazol) aumentan niveles de estatinas.
Fibratos y niacina aumentan riesgo de rabdomiólisis.
Suplementos de pomelo inhiben CYP3A4 y elevan concentración plasmática.
nursing_care: Verificar función hepática (ALT/AST) antes de iniciar y cada 3‑6 meses.
Evaluar dolor muscular, debilidad o cambios en la orina.
Monitorear CK y creatinina si aparecen síntomas musculares.
Retener la dosis si ALT/AST >3× límite normal o CK >10× normal y notificar al médico.
patient_teaching: Tomar la estatina a la misma hora cada día, preferiblemente por la noche.
Informar cualquier dolor muscular persistente o debilidad.
Evitar el consumo de pomelo y suplementos sin consultar al profesional.
Mantener hidratación adecuada y acudir a controles de laboratorio.

outcomes: Función renal: creatinina sérica ≤1.2 mg/dL en 48 h.
Integridad muscular: ausencia de dolor muscular o debilidad.

interventions.action: Monitorear CK y creatinina sérica cada 24 h si aparecen síntomas musculares.
interventions.rationale: Detectar rabdomiólisis temprana y prevenir daño renal.

interventions.action: Evaluar dolor muscular, debilidad y color de la orina en cada turno.
Fomentar ingesta de líquidos ≥2 L/día, salvo contraindicación.
interventions.rationale: Mantener perfusión renal y facilitar eliminación de mioglobina.

interventions.action: Retener la estatina y notificar al médico si CK >10× normal o ALT/AST >3× límite.
Documentar y comunicar cambios en laboratorio y síntomas al equipo de salud.
interventions.rationale: Garantizar intervención oportuna y coordinación del cuidado.

en.summary: Statins inhibit HMG‑CoA reductase, reducing hepatic LDL‑cholesterol synthesis and providing pleiotropic anti‑inflammatory and plaque‑stabilizing effects.
key_points: Pleiotropic effects: anti‑inflammatory, antioxidant, plaque stabilizer.
Common adverse effects: myalgia, rhabdomyolysis, transaminase elevation.
Contraindicated in pregnancy, lactation, and active liver disease.

mechanism: Inhibit HMG‑CoA reductase, blocking conversion of HMG‑CoA to mevalonate.
Decrease hepatic cholesterol production and upregulate LDL receptors.
Increased hepatic LDL‑c uptake lowers plasma concentration.
indications: Primary and secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
contraindications: Active liver disease (ALT/AST >3× upper limit of normal).
adverse_effects: Rhabdomyolysis (serious) → CK >10× normal, severe muscle pain, dark urine.
interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, itraconazole) increase statin levels.
Fibrates and niacin increase rhabdomyolysis risk.
Grapefruit supplements inhibit CYP3A4 and raise plasma concentration.
nursing_care: Check liver function (ALT/AST) before starting and every 3‑6 months.
Assess for muscle pain, weakness, or changes in urine.
Monitor CK and creatinine if muscular symptoms appear.
Hold dose if ALT/AST >3× upper limit or CK >10× normal and notify provider.
patient_teaching: Take statin at the same time each day, preferably at night.
Report any persistent muscle pain or weakness.
Avoid grapefruit and supplements without consulting a professional.
Maintain adequate hydration and attend lab follow‑ups.

outcomes: Renal function: serum creatinine ≤1.2 mg/dL within 48 h.
Muscle integrity: absence of muscle pain or weakness.

interventions.action: Monitor CK and serum creatinine every 24 h if muscular symptoms appear.
interventions.rationale: Detect early rhabdomyolysis and prevent renal damage.

interventions.action: Assess muscle pain, weakness, and urine color each shift.
Encourage fluid intake ≥2 L/day, unless contraindicated.
interventions.rationale: Maintain renal perfusion and facilitate myoglobin elimination.

interventions.action: Hold statin and notify provider if CK >10× normal or ALT/AST >3× upper limit.
Document and communicate lab changes and symptoms to the health team.
interventions.rationale: Ensure timely intervention and coordinated care.

summary.0.quote: Statins are oral drugs that work by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, which is an enzyme used in cholesterol synthesis.

key_points.1.quote: Some examples of pleiotropic effects are anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antiproliferative, and plaque-stabilizing actions, which contribute to their efficacy in preventing and treating CAD (Choudhary et al., 2023).

key_points.3.quote: Previously, statin medications carried a strong warning against use in pregnancy and were considered absolutely contraindicated.

sections.contraindications.1.quote: Previously, statin medications carried a strong warning against use in pregnancy and were considered absolutely contraindicated.

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Myalgia, or muscle pain, is common and occurred in 5%–10% of clients taking statin therapy in observational studies (Grundy et al., 2019).

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: Infrequently, statins have been associated with elevations in transaminase.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: However, in 2012 the FDA revised the recommendation for monitoring liver function and now recommends that liver enzymes be tested before starting statin therapy and only as clinically indicated thereafter.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Report any muscular signs and symptoms to their health care provider, including muscle pain, muscle weakness, and very dark urine, which can indicate rhabdomyolysis.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Unlike some other statins, rosuvastatin may be taken at any time of the day because it has a long half-life of 19 hours.
